episode_title: 35 Legendary Stars Still With Us in 2026 — Can You Recognize Them Now? | Then & Now 2026
counter_rule: Keep count of how many faces you remember. Comment your number.

cold_open.text: Welcome to Golden Hour — Hollywood, Then and Now. Some faces never really leave us. You hear one song, one laugh, one famous line, and a whole afternoon of your childhood comes rushing back. Tonight: thirty-five of the brightest stars of the sixties, seventies and eighties — and every single one of them is still with us in 2026. So keep count of how many you still remember. And stay to the very end — because the final name on our list owns a record twenty-one Oscar nominations. The category, as always, is Meryl.

acts.card_subtitle: Those We Never Forgot — The Movie Stars
acts.intro: Act One: Those We Never Forgot — the movie stars who owned the big screen. And we begin with a man who, in December of 2025, did something only a handful of performers in Hollywood history have ever done.

acts.card_subtitle: The Faces in Our Living Room
acts.intro: Act Two: The Faces in Our Living Room. Movies were events — but television was family. These faces sat across our dinner tables for twenty years, and every one of them is still with us.
Act Three: The Soundtrack of Our Lives. Before playlists, there were radios — and these are the voices that lived inside them. Every one of them still breathing.
Act Four: Still Turning Heads. Some stars faded. These didn't. Eight living proofs that the seventies never really ended.

memory_breaks.text: Quick pause. That's seventeen faces so far. How many did you remember? Drop your number in the comments — then stay right there, because the voices are next. Act Three begins now.
That's twenty-seven, and you're doing great. If you've recognized every single one, type STILL SHARP in the comments. One act left — and it belongs to the biggest names in the business.

outro.text: And that's thirty-five. Thirty-five faces time didn't erase. Before we go — this past year, Golden Hour said goodbye to Dolly Parton, Robert Duvall, Sam Neill, Chuck Norris and Tim Curry. The screen gets quieter every year. But tonight proved something too: thirty-five legends, still here, still shining at golden hour. So — how many did you remember? Leave your number in the comments, and subscribe, because part two is already loading: the dames and knights across the pond. Golden hour never really ends. It just waits for us to look up.

stars.name: Dick Van Dyke
stars.claim: Mary Poppins (1964), The Dick Van Dyke Show, Diagnosis: Murder
stars.narration: Put him in a chimney-sweep's cap and a cockney grin, and Mary Poppins plays in your head all over again. But Bert was only the beginning — five decades of television followed, from The Dick Van Dyke Show to Diagnosis: Murder. At 98, he became the oldest performer ever to win an Emmy. And in December 2025, Dick Van Dyke blew out one hundred candles — still dancing, still grinning, still ours.
verify: oldest Emmy winner at 98 (Creative Arts Emmys 2024, Days of Our Lives)

stars.name: Eva Marie Saint
stars.claim: On the Waterfront (1954), North by Northwest (1959)
stars.narration: You may remember the woman holding Cary Grant's hand on the train in North by Northwest. But the Oscar came earlier — On the Waterfront, 1954, opposite Brando. She never played the starlet; she played the woman who knew too much. Born on the Fourth of July, 1924, Eva Marie Saint is one hundred and two years old — the oldest living Oscar winner on Earth. The Academy's living legend, still writing her story.

stars.name: Clint Eastwood
stars.claim: The Man with No Name, Dirty Harry, Unforgiven, Million Dollar Baby
stars.narration: A cigar, a squint, three dollar bills — the Man with No Name didn't need dialogue to own the screen. Dirty Harry made him an icon; the director's chair made him immortal — four Oscars, from Unforgiven to Million Dollar Baby. Clint Eastwood turned 96 in May. His son says the Old Man has finally retired. After seventy years in front of and behind the camera — he's earned every silent sunset.
verify: son Kyle said retired (Nov 2025 video, resurfaced Jun 2026)

stars.name: Sophia Loren
stars.claim: Two Women (1961) — first acting Oscar for a foreign-language performance
stars.narration: One look from her, and you understood why the whole world fell for Italian cinema. She was a war child from the slums of Naples — and in 1961, Two Women made her the first actress ever to win an Oscar for a foreign-language performance. At 91, Sophia Loren remains the last great lady of Europe's golden screen — crowned in 2020 by one final, unforgettable performance in The Life Ahead.
verify: age 91 as of Sep 6 2026 (turns 92 on Sep 20)
alive as of Jun 2026 per Reddit; recheck before publish

stars.name: Julie Andrews
stars.claim: Mary Poppins (1964), The Sound of Music (1965)
stars.narration: Just one octave of Supercalifragilistic, or one hilltop of Salzburg, and you can hear her instantly. Then, in 1997, the voice that defined two generations was silenced by surgery. Hollywood braced for tragedy — instead, she built a second act: The Princess Diaries, and the voice of Lady Whistledown narrating Bridgerton. Dame Julie Andrews turned 90 last October — proof that even when the singing stops, the music doesn't.
verify: alive as of Feb 2026 per BuzzFeed; recheck

stars.name: Rita Moreno
stars.claim: West Side Story (1961) — Oscar; EGOT
stars.narration: In 1961, Anita danced through West Side Story like a flame — and took home the Oscar. Sixty years later, Steven Spielberg handed her a new role in the very same story — making her the only performer to appear in both versions of a Best Picture winner. Ninety-four years old, an EGOT before the term even existed, Rita Moreno is still onstage — because standing still was never part of her choreography.
verify: alive as of Feb 2026 per BuzzFeed; recheck

stars.name: Jane Fonda
stars.claim: Barbarella, Klute, Coming Home, Grace and Frankie
stars.narration: Barbarella in space, Bree Daniels on the phone — in the seventies, Jane Fonda was the most fearless woman on screen. Two Oscars later — Klute, Coming Home — she traded the screen for protest lines, and paid for it: the lists, the arrests, the nickname. At 88, she is still marching — climate protests, bare-knuckle activism, Grace and Frankie reruns. Hollywood trained her to perform. She chose to fight.

stars.name: Kim Novak
stars.claim: Vertigo (1958), Picnic, Bell Book and Candle
stars.narration: That grey suit at the foot of the stairs. Vertigo made Kim Novak the most mysterious blonde of the fifties — Madeleine and Judy, the same woman twice. But Hollywood was a world she chose to leave: painting, poetry, horses, and a quiet life in Oregon, far from the spotlight that nearly broke her. At 93, Venice honored her with a Golden Lion for lifetime achievement. She came back on her own terms — and then went home.
verify: alive as of Jun 26 2026 per Reddit thread; recheck

stars.name: William Shatner
stars.claim: Star Trek (1966–69), T.J. Hooker, Boston Legal
stars.narration: Space — the final frontier. You cannot read that line in any other voice. Typecast forever as Kirk, he bent the typecast: T. J. Hooker, Denny Crane, the Priceline pitchman with a wink. At ninety, William Shatner flew to actual space — and came home changed. Now ninety-five, he still tours, still records, still boldly goes.

stars.name: Carol Burnett
stars.claim: The Carol Burnett Show (1967–78)
stars.narration: One tug of that curtain-rod earring, and The Carol Burnett Show made America laugh before dinner. Eleven seasons, a Tarzan yell that still stops traffic, and a generosity that built a comedy dynasty. At ninety-three, Carol Burnett remains the first lady of television comedy — and still never takes herself too seriously.

stars.name: Angie Dickinson
stars.claim: Rio Bravo (1959), Police Woman (1974–78)
stars.narration: Feathers, the card-playing beauty of Rio Bravo. Twenty years later she flipped the script: Police Woman made Pepper Anderson the first woman to headline a hit cop show. This very month, Angie Dickinson turns ninety-five — rarely photographed, famously picky, and still the coolest face of the seventies.
verify: alive per 2026 death-list cross-check; recheck — LOW public visibility

stars.name: Alan Alda
stars.claim: M*A*S*H (1972–83) — Hawkeye Pierce
stars.narration: M*A*S*H gave television its greatest joke-teller and its deepest wound, and Alan Alda carried both for eleven seasons. Then he built a second life teaching empathy — to doctors, to engineers, one conversation at a time. At ninety, he still hosts, still writes, still asks the better question.

stars.name: Barbara Eden
stars.claim: I Dream of Jeannie (1965–70)
stars.narration: The blink. The ponytail. The pink harem pants. Five seasons of I Dream of Jeannie made her immortal in syndication. At ninety-five, Barbara Eden still greets convention crowds with the arms-crossed nod — and fans still ask for the wish she invented sixty years ago. She always grants it.

stars.name: Tina Louise
stars.claim: Gilligan's Island (1964–67) — Ginger Grant
stars.narration: Ginger Grant — the movie star stranded on a three-hour tour. When the island went off the air, Tina Louise walked away from Ginger forever: no reunions, no sequels. At ninety-two, she is the last islander still with us, having outlived every single castmate. She made it home.

stars.name: Marla Gibbs
stars.claim: The Jeffersons (Florence), 227
stars.narration: For a decade, Florence kept the Jeffersons' penthouse honest, one withering look at George at a time. Then she produced 227 into a hit nobody believed in. At ninety-five, Marla Gibbs is still booking roles — steady work across eight decades. Moving on up.

stars.name: Mike Farrell
stars.claim: M*A*S*H — B.J. Hunnicutt (1975–83)
stars.narration: He replaced a legend on television's toughest stage — B. J. Hunnicutt stepping into the 4077th and making us stop missing Trapper. Off camera he became television's conscience: prison reform, human rights, refugee missions. Fifty years on — with Shelley by his side — Mike Farrell simply will not sit down.

stars.name: Jaclyn Smith
stars.claim: Charlie's Angels (1976–81) — Kelly Garrett
stars.narration: Kelly Garrett — the calm center of Charlie's Angels, the only Angel who answered every single call. Then she built a fashion empire from a Kmart rack, worth hundreds of millions. At eighty, Jaclyn Smith still posts the elegance that made the seventies stand up straight.
verify: only Angel in all 110 eps + 2019 cameo

stars.name: Willie Nelson
stars.claim: On the Road Again, Crazy, outlaw country founder, Farm Aid
stars.narration: One beat-up guitar named Trigger, one bandana, a voice like a Texas gravel road. Nashville shut him out, so he invented outlaw country — then built Farm Aid into a forty-year promise. At ninety-three, Willie Nelson is still recording. The road goes on forever. So does he.

stars.name: Johnny Mathis
stars.claim: Chances Are, Misty, 70+ albums
stars.narration: Chances are — two syllables, and forty years of school dances come flooding back. In 2025, after nearly seventy years on the road, Johnny Mathis said goodbye to touring. This month he turns ninety-one. The voice stepped back; the man didn't. Chances are, he's still humming.
verify: retired from touring (announced Mar 2025, final shows May 2025)

stars.name: Tom Jones
stars.claim: It's Not Unusual, Delilah, Sex Bomb
stars.narration: The hips, the sweat, It's Not Unusual — and a rain of lingerie over Las Vegas. The sex symbol outlived the seventies by simply being a singer. At eighty-six, Sir Tom Jones still tours, still coaches on The Voice, and still dares you to sit down during Delilah.

stars.name: Frankie Valli
stars.claim: The Four Seasons — Sherry, Big Girls Don't Cry, Can't Take My Eyes Off You
stars.narration: That falsetto — Sherry, Big Girls Don't Cry, Can't Take My Eyes Off You. Jersey street kids who outsold the British Invasion at home. At eighty-nine, Frankie Valli became a father again — to twins. Now ninety-two, he is still onstage. Oh, what a night. He keeps having them.

stars.name: Dionne Warwick
stars.claim: Walk On By, Say a Little Prayer, That's What Friends Are For
stars.narration: Four notes of Walk On By, and Burt Bacharach's whole songbook walks through the door. In her eighties she became the warmest, funniest woman on social media. Dionne Warwick is eighty-five — still touring, still reading your comments, still that voice.

stars.name: Neil Diamond
stars.claim: Sweet Caroline, Cracklin' Rosie, I Am... I Said
stars.narration: Sweet Caroline — three chords, one ba-ba-ba, and every stadium on Earth becomes a choir. Parkinson's ended the touring, never the songs. Broadway built A Beautiful Noise around him, and on opening night he stood up and sang along. At eighty-five, the melody never shakes.
verify: A Beautiful Noise opening Jun 2022 surprise singalong

stars.name: Paul Anka
stars.claim: Diana, My Way (for Sinatra), Johnny's Theme
stars.narration: At sixteen he wrote Diana, and it sold nine million copies before he could legally drive. Then came My Way for Sinatra, the Tonight Show theme, hits for Michael Jackson. At eighty-five, Paul Anka still plays Las Vegas — the last of the great songmen.

stars.name: Shirley Bassey
stars.claim: Goldfinger, Diamonds Are Forever, Moonraker
stars.narration: GOLD-finger. One word — held, belted, immortal — and James Bond found his golden voice. Goldfinger, Diamonds Are Forever, Moonraker: three themes across three decades, and no other singer has ever carried even two. Dame Shirley Bassey is eighty-nine. The diamonds are forever. So is she.

stars.name: Herb Alpert
stars.claim: Tijuana Brass, A&M Records, Rise (1979)
stars.narration: That warm brass fanfare — the Tijuana Brass outselling the Beatles in 1966. The label he built became home to the Carpenters and the Police — and then he gave his fortune away, to teach the next generation music. At ninety-one, Herb Alpert still paints, sculpts and records. Rise never really ends.
verify: alive per 2026 death-list cross-check; recheck — LOW visibility

stars.name: Nancy Sinatra
stars.claim: These Boots Are Made for Walkin' (1966), Somethin' Stupid duet
stars.narration: Go-go boots on a candy-colored soundstage — the sassiest warning shot of 1966. A year later she recorded Somethin' Stupid with her father, still the only father-daughter duet ever to reach number one. Nancy Sinatra is eighty-six — still walking it her way.

stars.name: Jack Nicholson
stars.claim: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest, The Shining, As Good as It Gets
stars.narration: Here's Johnny! — an axe through a door, and the most famous grin in movies. Three Oscars, twelve nominations — then, around 2010, the greatest recluse in Hollywood simply stopped. No farewell tour. No explanation. At eighty-nine, Jack Nicholson surfaces at Lakers games — gray beard, sunglasses, that same grin.
verify: alive per 2026 death-list cross-check; recheck — LOW visibility

stars.name: Harrison Ford
stars.claim: Star Wars, Indiana Jones, Blade Runner, 1923
stars.narration: A smuggler's smirk in a cantina — Han Solo was never the hero; he was something better: a survivor. A carpenter turned superstar, a legend who walked away from two real plane crashes. At eighty-four, Harrison Ford is still first on the call sheet. The fedora fits. It always will.

stars.name: Cher
stars.claim: Sonny & Cher Show, Moonstruck, Believe
stars.narration: Half of Sonny and Cher, in bell-bottoms and deadpan. Then the reinventions: an Oscar for Moonstruck, the Believe vocal that rewired pop, a farewell tour now twenty years long. Cher turned eighty this May — the only artist with a number-one single in seven consecutive decades. Goddesses don't retire.

stars.name: Goldie Hawn
stars.claim: Laugh-In, Private Benjamin, Overboard
stars.narration: That giggle on Laugh-In — the dumb blonde who was always the smartest person in the room. An Oscar at twenty-four, thirty years of pure star power, and forty years with Kurt Russell without a single wedding. At eighty, Goldie Hawn laughs exactly like 1968 — and refuses, on principle, to act her age.

stars.name: Bette Midler
stars.claim: The Divine Miss M, Wind Beneath My Wings, Hocus Pocus
stars.narration: The Divine Miss M — bathhouse sass, Wind Beneath My Wings, every tear-jerker your mother played twice. Then she took stardom to the streets, replanting New York's community gardens block by block. At eighty, Bette Midler still sings like a weather system. Some stars twinkle. The Divine One illuminates.

stars.name: Lily Tomlin
stars.claim: Laugh-In (Ernestine), 9 to 5, Grace and Frankie
stars.narration: Ernestine, the telephone operator — one ringy-dingy — the funniest switchboard in America. Nine to Five, then Grace and Frankie made her a legend twice over. At eighty-seven, Lily Tomlin still tours new material with her wife and partner Jane Wagner. She sounds like she's just getting started.

stars.name: Al Pacino
stars.claim: The Godfather, Scarface, Scent of a Woman
stars.narration: Say hello to my little friend. You heard it in his voice before the sentence ended. The Godfather, Scarface, an Oscar finally with Scent of a Woman. At eighty-six, Al Pacino is a father again — his youngest son born when he was eighty-three. Michael Corleone left the family business. Al never wanted out.

stars.name: Meryl Streep
stars.claim: Sophie's Choice, Kramer vs. Kramer, The Devil Wears Prada
stars.narration: Sophie's Choice — one scene, and cinema redefined what acting could cost. A record twenty-one nominations, three Oscars — from Miranda Priestly's withering stare to Only Murders in the Building. At seventy-seven, Meryl Streep stole a comedy after conquering five decades of drama. The category is acting. It was always Meryl.
